items.headline: Nvidia reports $115.8B quarterly revenue, up 103% year over year, and guides next quarter to $130B
items.why: Data center revenue of $107.6B (up 110%) shows AI infrastructure spending still accelerating, and the guide implies roughly 12% sequential growth from an already enormous base.

items.headline: Nvidia shares reversed from a 2.7% pre-open gain to close down 2.9% despite the beat
items.why: A stock that sells off on a beat-and-raise tells you expectations were already priced in, so the AI trade now needs more than good numbers to move higher.

items.headline: Bitcoin slips to about $63,600 after Fed minutes show the October hold was a close call
items.why: The FOMC held at 3.75%-4% on a 10-2 vote with two members wanting a hike, and December hike odds near 90% keep pressure on a risk asset with no yield.

items.headline: Bitcoin fell about 9% in the week to Nov 13, reaching roughly $62,100 on Sunday
items.why: The drop came as the 10-year Treasury yield jumped to about 5.14% from 4.86%, reinforcing that crypto is trading as a rates-sensitive asset right now.

items.headline: October Fed minutes: almost all officials judged further rate rises likely appropriate
items.why: The committee is leaning toward continued tightening, and futures price roughly a 95% chance of a quarter-point hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting.

items.headline: US October PPI came in at 6.5% year over year versus 6.6% expected, but two Fed officials still signalled more hikes
items.why: A marginally cooler print did not change the policy path, and the 10-year yield rose to about 5.14% that day, tightening financial conditions further.

items.headline: Spot gold falls about 3.3% to near $3,723, its lowest level since September 2025; silver drops about 5%
items.why: Hawkish minutes, a dollar index near its highest since April 2025 and a 10-year yield around 5.07% raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding metals.

items.why: A much larger-than-expected inventory build undercuts the supply-risk premium, while Brent at $91.95 still sits well above WTI.
